key_insight: An enhanced PINN-based quantum optimal control method can match established solvers like Krotov and PRONTO while achieving high-fidelity gate control with low leakage in multi-level quantum systems.
engineering_relevance: This work points to a scalable, physics-guided route for automating pulse design and hardware characterization in future quantum processors.
method: Uses Fourier feature embeddings to reduce spectral bias in oscillatory quantum dynamics.
Adds dynamic epoch normalization and informed pre-training to stabilize PINN training.
Benchmarks against Krotov and PRONTO on fluxonium and NV-center gate control tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gate fidelities above 99.9% with suppressed population leakage and compares computational time, iteration efficiency, and mean leakage across methods.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful tuning of the enhanced PINN components and may still face scaling challenges for larger quantum systems or stricter phase constraints.
paper_title: Performance of Krotov, PRONTO and PINN for optimal control of quantum gates
